full_judgment:
2. Facts, in short are that the plaintiffs petitioners filed Title Suit No. 839/18 in the court of 2nd Court Munsif, Jessore for a declaration to the effect that the suit land where a cattle market sits once in a week is not a hat within the meaning under section 2 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and as such is not acquirable under the provisions of the said Act. It was further case of plaintiffs that no compensation assessment roll has been prepared and published in respect of the suit land and as such the order of acquisition is illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs, Plaintiff filed an application under Order 39 rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for an order of temporary injunction restraining the defdts from dispossessing the plaintiffs from the suit land and from shifting the cattle market from its place to any other place till the disposal of the suit The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter alia that the suit land in question is a regular hat within the meaning of section 2 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and it has been legally acquired as per-provisions of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. It was farther contended by the defendant that the compensation assessment roll in respect of the suit land has already-finally been published and as such the suit land was rightly acquired. As to the prayer of temporary injunction defendants submitted that the prayer for temporary injunction should not be granted. 

 3. Mr. Syed Shamsur Rahman, the learned Advocate has appeared on behalf of the petitioners. He submits that both the courts below committed an error of law dismissing the suit of the plaintiffs inasmuch as the order of acquisition of the suit land is wholly illegal as the suit land is not a hat in accordance with the provision of East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. He further submits that as the compensation assessment roll has not been prepared the acquisition of the land in question alleged to be a hat is not legal. 

 4. Mr. M.A. Wahab, the learned Assistant Attorney General has appeared on behalf of the opposite parties, He submits that the order of acquisition in respect of the suit land is a valid and legal one, and as such it cannot be disturbed. According to him compensation assessment roll has already been published as per provision of the State Acquisition Act on 26th October, 1978, and as such there has been no illegality in passing the order of Acquisition. In support of his contention Mr. M.A Wahab has referred to two decisions reported in 25 DLR at pages 248 and 476, He has also referred to a decision reported in 16 DLR (SC) page 281. 

 5. It is the case of the plaintiffs that the suit land has been illegally acquired by the Government and as such that order should be set aside. According to the plaintiffs the suit land is not liable to be acquired by the Government as compensation assessment roll in respect of the suit has not yet been prepared. On the other hand, the Government contested the suit contending inter alia that the Government has acquired the suit land as per provision of East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and compensation assessment roll in respect of the suit land has already been published as such there has been no illegality committed in acquiring the suit land. In the case of Prove of E. Pak Vs. The Secretary Muktazacha Abbasia Sbnr. Madrassa reported in 16 DLR (SC) page 281, it has been held:- 

 "Reading the Act as a whole the intention appears to be firstly. that all rent receiving interests shall disappear; secondly, that so far as tenants are concerned, they will be entitled to retain possession only of certain categories of lands which are retainable, and thirdly, that even in respect of such retainable lands a maxim celling is fixed. 

 "So far as the rent receivers are concerned, their interests are to vest either from the date of the Notification of acquisition or from the date mentioned in such a notification. But so far as tenants were concerned, their interests are to stand acquired, and vested in Government on the notification of the final publication of the compensation assessment roll. 

 From the above quotation it is abundantly clear that the hats and bazars belonging to the rent receiver vested in the Government from the date of notification of acquisition and hats and bazars belonging to the tenant and rayaits vested in the Government on and from the date of final publication of compensation assessment roll. In the present case the compensation assessment roll has been prepared and published in the Bangladesh Gazette dated 26th Oct. 1978, as such the hat in question vested in the Government from the date. In this connection reference may be made to the case reported in 25 D.L.R page 284 in the case of Provo of E Pakistan Vs. Md. Shahabuddin Gazi and others wherein it was held :- 

 "Hats and bazars belonging to the rent receivers vested in the Government with effect from' the date of the notification in 1956 and so far as raiyats, etc. are concerned vesting took place after the final publication of the compensation under section 44(3)2". 

 6. From this decision also it is clear that the hats and bazars belonging to the rent receivers vested in the Government with effect from the date of notification and the hats and bazars belonging to the rayats vested in the Government after final publication of compensation assessment roll. 

 7. In the present case whole question is whether hat in question has been legally acquired or vested in the Government or not. In view of the above noted decisions it can easily be said that the hat in question has vested in the Government after final publication of the assessment roll on 26.10.78. In this view of the matter I do not find any substance in the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioners.
